e.meaning: from the River Shannon; possessor of wisdom
e.etymology: A spelling of Shannon, from Sionainn, the Irish name of the River Shannon, usually explained as possessor of wisdom. It peaked in the early 1990s with the actress Shannen Doherty.
namesakes: Shannen Doherty (actress, Beverly Hills 90210 and Charmed)

assoc.t: Shannen Doherty, actress in Beverly Hills, 90210

e.etymology: In Greek, Veta is a short form of Elisavet (Elizabeth). The source of the American name of the early 1900s is not recorded; it sits beside Veda, Vita and Reta.
A variant of Hayward, the medieval officer who kept fences and hedges in repair, from Old English hege (hedge) and weard (guard). Heyward is the spelling of an old South Carolina family.
A variant of Spanish Consuelo, consolation, from the title of the Virgin Mary Nuestra Senora del Consuelo, Our Lady of Consolation.

assoc.t: Consuela, the deadpan housekeeper on Family Guy

e.note: In Spanish the usual form is Consuelo, for women too; Consuela is mainly an English-language variant.

e.etymology: An English surname that began as a nickname for a new arrival in a place, new plus man.

assoc.t: Newman, Jerry's mail-carrier nemesis on Seinfeld
Paul Newman, actor and Newman's Own founder

e.etymology: A compound in the manner of Marilee and Marylee, respelled with merry. It sounds like the adverb merrily.
A form that sits between Helen and Elaine. Elaine is itself an Old French form of Helen, so all three go back to Greek Helene, traditionally linked with a word for torch.
A respelling of Florence, from Latin Florentia, built on florens, flowering or flourishing. Florence Nightingale, named for the Italian city of her birth, made it popular.
A variant of Alvina, the feminine form of Alvin, from Old English Aelfwine, elf friend, and related Germanic names.
From Latin Leonia, a feminine name built on leo, lion, and an equivalent of Leona. In Polish it is also a short form of Leonarda.
An American elaboration of Lori or Laura that echoes Gloria. Loria is also an Italian, Spanish and Jewish surname.
A short American name of the 1960s and 1970s in the pattern of Lisa and Tisha. In Slovene, Tisa is a separate women's name.
A variant of Darlene, a 20th-century coinage from the word darling, shaped like Charlene and Marlene.
An English surname, a variant of Collins, from Colin, a medieval pet form of Nicholas. American use as a first name owes much to the railroad magnate Collis P. Huntington.
A respelling of Marilyn, a 20th-century blend of Mary and Lynn.
An American name of the 1970s built on the Sha- opening, close in sound to Sharon and Shalonda.
A pet form of Lydia, given as a full name in the late 1800s. Lydia is Greek for a woman from Lydia, an ancient region of Asia Minor, and is a New Testament name.
An English place name and surname, Old English Bedanford, the river crossing of a man named Beda or Bede.
A Scottish surname from the personal name Ewen, the English form of Gaelic Eoghann.

assoc.t: The Ewings, the oil family of TV's Dallas
Patrick Ewing, Hall of Fame Knicks center

e.note: Ewing sarcoma, a bone cancer that mostly affects children and teens, carries the same name.

e.etymology: A respelling of Lorraine, the region of eastern France, whose name comes from Lotharingia, the kingdom of Lothar.
A 1930s American name that gives Arlene and Darlene an H, sometimes used as a feminine form of Harlan or Harley.
Taken from Lafayette, the title of the French general who fought in the American Revolution, and long a men's name. Recent use is for girls, where it reads as Faye with the -ette ending.
An English surname for someone who lived by a beech tree. As a first name it honored the preacher Henry Ward Beecher, brother of Harriet Beecher Stowe, and peaked the year after he died in 1887.
Vietnamese Hung, written with tone marks, is the Sino-Vietnamese reading of characters meaning heroic and brave, or in another tone prosperous. Hung is also a Chinese surname.
e.note: In English hung is the past tense of hang and a crude slang word, so jokes are likely.

assoc.t: hung, past tense of hang; slang for well-endowed

e.etymology: An English surname from a medieval everyday form of Horace, the Roman family name Horatius. Orris is also the fragrant iris root used in perfume.
A respelling of Harvey, from the Breton name Haerviu, battle worthy, which Bretons brought to England with the Norman Conquest.
A spelling of Loreto, the Italian town whose shrine of the Holy House made its name a Catholic given name. The place name comes from Latin lauretum, laurel grove.
A form of Jamal, from Arabic jamal, beauty. The Je- spelling is the usual one in Ethiopia and Georgia, and matches Turkish Cemal.
